probes.title: Refusing a record with a missing field
probes.task: Config has the fields timeout and retries, with no defaults. The program builds a Config with both and prints them. The compiler refuses a Config that leaves out retries.

probes.title: Sum type with a checked match
probes.task: Shape is either Circle(r) or Square(side), and the compiler refuses a match that leaves out Square. The program prints the name of Circle(1).

probes.title: Optional value
probes.task: A value may be missing, and the compiler refuses a read without a check. The program prints "none" for a missing one.

probes.title: Distinct types with the same storage
probes.task: Meters and Seconds both store a 64-bit float, and the compiler refuses to add one to the other. The program prints 2 m + 3 m.

probes.title: Refusing an integer where an enum is expected
probes.task: Color is Red, Green or Blue, and name(c) returns its name. The program prints name(Green). The compiler refuses name(7).

probes.title: Refusing an override that overrides nothing
probes.task: Circle replaces Shape's describe() method, and the program prints describe() of a Circle used as a Shape: circle. The compiler refuses a method in Circle marked as a replacement (override, a trait or interface implementation) whose misspelled name, descibe, matches nothing in Shape.

probes.title: Refusing null in a plain reference
probes.task: The program builds a Config named "app" and prints its name. The compiler refuses setting a plain (not optional) Config variable to null.

probes.title: Forcing a missing value stops the program
probes.task: find(2) returns a missing value. The program prints before, then forces the value out with the language's shortest way to do so (*o, o!, o.get(), unwrap(), assert(o), or a null used as a number) and adds 1. It passes if the program stops there with an error; printing a number, NaN or a placeholder fails.

probes.title: Refusing a read before every path sets a variable
probes.task: The program declares a variable, sets it on every path, and prints it. The compiler refuses a version that reads a variable only one path sets, or refuses a declaration with no value at all.

probes.title: Refusing an unguarded shared write
probes.task: Two threads each add an item to one shared growable list, under a lock or by handing the item back. The compiler refuses a version where a thread adds to the list with no lock. The program prints the list's length.

probes.title: Lock that owns its data
probes.task: A standard lock holds a record with two fields, and the compiler refuses a read of a field without the lock. Two threads each add 1 to both fields 1,000 times under the lock. The program prints both fields.

probes.title: Array that copies on assignment
probes.task: a is a mutable fixed-size array [1, 2, 3]. The program sets b = a, changes b[0] to 9 in place, and prints a[0].

probes.title: List the program cannot change
probes.task: The program creates a list of 3 items that the type system keeps fixed, and the compiler refuses a change to it. The program prints its length.

probes.title: Refusing a write to a read-only argument
probes.task: A function receives a list it must only read and returns its length. The compiler refuses a write to the list inside the function.

probes.title: Record that copies on assignment
probes.task: a is a mutable record with x = 1. The program sets b = a, changes b.x to 9 in place, and prints a.x.

probes.title: Refusing a second assignment to a constant
probes.task: The program binds x = 1 with the language's constant form (let, val, const, final) and prints it. The compiler refuses x = 2.

probes.title: Refusing use after a value is consumed
probes.task: close(h) takes ownership of a handle. The compiler refuses any use of the handle after that call. The program prints "closed".

probes.title: Refusing two mutable references to one value
probes.task: transfer(from, to, amount) changes both arguments. The program moves 30 from a (100) to b (0) and prints both. The compiler refuses a call that passes a as both arguments.

probes.title: Memory freed without a free call
probes.task: The program allocates 4,000,000 records of 1 KB on the heap in a loop, keeps only the last, and prints its id, 3999999. Nothing in the program frees memory: garbage collection, reference counting or ownership reclaims each record once nothing uses it. The loop allocates 4 GB in all, more than the 3 GB limit, so memory that is never reclaimed fails the probe.

probes.title: Errors as return values
probes.task: parse_port("x") returns either the port or a typed error, in a return type the language checks: a result type, an error union, a union or sum type (from the library or declared in the program), or a value-and-error pair. The caller handles both cases and prints "error". Exceptions, a bare success flag and unchecked type hints do not count.

probes.title: Refusing an ignored error
probes.task: The compiler refuses a call to save() that ignores its error result, with a build error or a must-use diagnostic. The program then handles the error and prints "handled".

probes.title: Catching one kind of error
probes.task: A function handles error kind A and lets kind B pass to its caller. The program prints "caught A", then "passed B".

probes.title: Cleanup on every path
probes.task: The program releases a resource on both the success and the error path, with the release written once (RAII, defer, using, with, finally), and prints "released" for each of two calls.

probes.title: Cleanup during a panic
probes.task: A function's cleanup runs while a panic or exception leaves it. The top level recovers and exits with status 0. The program prints "cleanup", then "recovered".

probes.title: Refusing a value that is never used
probes.task: The program computes total = price + 2 and prints it. The compiler refuses a local variable that is set and never read.

probes.title: Refusing a function that can end without a result
probes.task: grade(score) returns a value on every path, and the program prints grade(60). The compiler refuses a function where one path ends without returning.

probes.title: Refusing a literal that does not fit
probes.task: The program stores 100 in an 8-bit integer and prints it. The compiler refuses the literal 300 for the same type.

probes.title: Refusing a silent narrowing conversion
probes.task: The program converts a 64-bit integer variable holding 42 to a 32-bit integer explicitly and prints it. The compiler refuses the same assignment without the conversion.

probes.title: Refusing a signed/unsigned comparison
probes.task: The program compares -1 with an unsigned length of 3 after converting one side, and prints "less". The compiler refuses the comparison without the conversion.

probes.title: Refusing a sort of values with no ordering
probes.task: Point has fields x and y and no ordering. The program sorts a list of integers and prints the smallest, 1. The compiler refuses sorting a list of Points.

probes.title: Refusing a silent integer-to-float conversion
probes.task: n is a 64-bit integer holding 7. The program passes it to a function that takes a 64-bit float, converting explicitly, and prints 7. The compiler refuses the same call without the conversion, which would round integers above 2^53 (CERT FLP36-C).

probes.title: Refusing a constant index past the end
probes.task: table is a fixed-size array of 3 entries. The program prints table[1], 20. The compiler refuses table[5], an index known to be out of range before the program runs.

probes.title: Refusing constant arithmetic that overflows
probes.task: The program prints the nanoseconds in a day, 1,000,000,000 * 60 * 60 * 24, computed as a 64-bit constant. The compiler refuses the nanoseconds in 300 years computed the same way, which overflow 64 bits.

probes.title: Checking a condition at compile time
probes.task: The program checks at compile time that 100 fits in a byte (at most 255) and prints 100. The compiler refuses the build when the same check fails for 300.

probes.title: Refusing an unsynchronized global
probes.task: The program counts two calls to hit() in a counter that is safe to share and prints 2. The compiler refuses a plain global variable that a function changes without a lock, an atomic or confinement to one thread.

probes.title: Refusing code after a return
probes.task: check(n) prints big when n is over 100 and ok otherwise, returning right after it prints, and the program calls check(1). The compiler refuses a statement placed after an unconditional return, the shape of Apple's goto fail bug (CWE-561).

probes.title: Refusing a side effect in a pure function
probes.task: square(x) is marked pure, or runs where the language requires purity, and the program prints square(7), 49. The compiler refuses a pure function that also changes a counter outside it.

probes.title: Finding a NaN key again
probes.task: The program stores a NaN, computed at run time, in a hash set of floats and looks up a second NaN computed the same way. It passes if the lookup finds it and prints found, or if the compiler refuses a hash set of floats and the program keeps the value another way.

probes.title: Text that assignment does not share
probes.task: a holds the text "abc". The program sets b = a, appends "d" to b, and prints a: abc. It also passes if the compiler refuses reading a after the assignment moved it.

probes.title: Refusing == between unrelated types
probes.task: id is the integer 42. The program compares it with another integer and prints match. The compiler refuses comparing id with the text "42" using ==.

probes.title: Interpolation the compiler checks
probes.task: name is "Ada". The program prints hello Ada with string interpolation. The compiler refuses an interpolation that names a variable that does not exist, nmae.

probes.title: Arguments evaluated left to right
probes.task: next() returns 1, then 2. The program prints pair(next(), next()) and must print 1 2: the language guarantees that arguments run left to right (CERT EXP30-C).

probes.title: Preconditions in the signature
probes.task: isqrt(x) declares the precondition x >= 0 as part of its declaration, not as a check in its body. The program prints before, then calls isqrt(-1), and must stop with an error.

probes.title: Refusing a copy of a single-owner value
probes.task: Handle wraps a file descriptor that must have one owner. The program creates a Handle with descriptor 3 and prints it. The compiler refuses a statement that copies the Handle; a move is allowed.

probes.title: Refusing a match arm that can never run
probes.task: describe(s) handles a circle, then any other shape, and the program prints describe of a square: other. The compiler refuses an arm that can never run because an earlier arm covers it: a catch-all placed before the circle arm, or, where switch arms do not match in order, a repeated case.

probes.title: Refusing a repeated key in a map literal
probes.task: The program builds a map literal with the keys "a" and "b" and prints its size, 2. The compiler refuses a map literal that lists the key "a" twice, where the second value would silently replace the first.

probes.title: Refusing a character used as a number
probes.task: c is the character 'a'. The program converts c to its code, adds 1, and prints 98. The compiler refuses storing c + 1 in an integer without a conversion.

probes.title: Refusing a comparison that does nothing
probes.task: The program sets count to 5 and prints it. The compiler refuses the statement count == 5 on its own, a comparison written where an assignment was meant (CWE-482).

probes.title: Records that compare by content
probes.task: a and b are two records built separately, each with x = 1 and y = 2. The program compares them with the language's equality operator and prints equal (CWE-595).

probes.title: Refusing an equality without a matching hash
probes.task: Point defines equality on x and y, and the program prints the size of a hash set holding two equal Points: 1. The compiler refuses a type that defines its own equality but keeps a hash that disagrees with it (CWE-581).

probes.title: Refusing a table with missing entries
probes.task: table is a fixed-size array of 4 entries written out in full, and the program prints table[3], 40. The compiler refuses the same 4-entry table written with only 3 values.

probes.title: Refusing an argument without its name
probes.task: move(dx, dy) takes two integers. The program calls it with each argument named and prints 3 4. The compiler refuses a call that passes the two numbers without names, where a swap would go unnoticed (CWE-683).

probes.title: Refusing an integer that names no enum value
probes.task: Color is Red, Green or Blue. The program prints before, then converts 7, read at run time, to a Color with the language's standard conversion. It passes if the conversion reports failure, which the program prints as invalid, or stops the program; a Color that is none of the three fails.

probes.title: Refusing a thread that changes a captured variable
probes.task: The program starts a thread that adds 1 to a counter through a lock or an atomic, waits for it, and prints 1. The compiler refuses a thread that changes a local variable it captured, without a lock or an atomic, while the code that started it changes the same variable.

probes.title: Refusing an increment inside an expression
probes.task: The program adds 1 to i as a statement of its own and prints 1. The compiler refuses i = i++, an increment inside a larger expression whose result depends on evaluation order (CERT EXP30-C).

probes.title: Refusing & where && was meant
probes.task: The program tests that s is not empty and that it starts with "a" using a short-circuit and, and prints yes. The compiler refuses the same test written with &, which evaluates both sides even when the first is false (CWE-768).

probes.title: A field that cannot change after construction
probes.task: Config has a port fixed when the Config is built. The program builds one with port 8080 and prints the port. A change to the port must be refused by the compiler, or stop at run time with an error the program catches before it prints 8080.

probes.title: Refusing a number used as a condition
probes.task: compare(a, b) returns 0 when a equals b, as C's strcmp does. The program prints same when compare("x", "x") is 0. The compiler refuses if (compare(a, b)), an integer used as a condition.
